sources.retrieval: Official article directly reviewed, including Top 5 ancestries by generation, 2021
sources.cohort: Australian resident census population, all ages; generation categories as defined by ABS
sources.unit: Percent of the respective generation population reporting an ancestry
sources.multiplicity: Up to two ancestry responses; rows overlap and are not exhaustive
sources.allowedUse: Demonstrate why family generation and multiple ancestry responses must remain separate from country of birth; extraction reference for a future compatible context model
limitations: Not athlete or male NFL-age frequencies
Not exclusive racial categories
No individual joint responses or appearance observations
Australian Aboriginal response category was added in 2021; question changes affect comparisons
No generation-specific sampling coefficients adopted

sources.observation: Natural hair shades vary with pigment type and amount, involve multiple genes, and can change with age
sources.allowedUse: Separate continuous natural pigment from dye and variable graying; preserve correlated but individually varied pigment channels
limitations: No country-by-age-by-athlete joint probabilities
The worldwide dark-hair estimate is not an NFL recruitment distribution
Renderer RGB mappings remain design assumptions

sources.observation: Hair texture and strand thickness have multiple influences; they are distinct traits
sources.allowedUse: Save curvature and thickness separately from density, length, cut and treatment
limitations: No complete national texture frequency table
No NFL grooming frequency measurements
No genotype-based simulator coefficients adopted

sources.observation: Iris color is a continuum influenced by multiple genes, including overlapping pigment influences with other tissues
sources.allowedUse: Vary shades within labels and retain supported cross-channel correlations without one fixed national palette
limitations: No national/NFL quantitative shade frequencies
No rule that all pigment channels must match
No rare-condition prevalence adopted

sources.retrieval: Primary indexed abstract excerpt reviewed; direct retrieval returned a disclosure footer
sources.observation: Iris-image blue/brown pixel counts produce a quantitative PIE-score rather than only broad color labels
sources.allowedUse: Motivate continuous iris variation and equal-lighting image comparisons
limitations: Full methods, sample details and observations not verified in this review
No PIE-score-to-renderer conversion adopted
Not world or NFL prevalence evidence

sources.collectionPeriod: 2010–2016 Combine participants, as stated in the abstract methods
sources.cohort: 1958 invited Combine participants completing air-displacement composition testing
sources.observation: BMI and measured composition classify substantially different obesity rates in this selected athlete sample
sources.allowedUse: Keep measured/estimated composition separate from height and weight; permit different compatible tissue distributions at the same size
limitations: Selected prospects rather than current active NFL players
No individual regional geometry or covariance extracted
Abstract results also mention 2017 despite methods ending in 2016; preserve discrepancy rather than invent a corrected collection period
No BMI-to-fat or physique coefficients adopted

sources.allowedUse: Separate season-wide participation, active-roster status, birthplace, childhood football location and recruitment pathway
limitations: No matching unique league denominator extracted
No complete country counts or country-by-identity cross-tab
No appearance frequencies
Do not divide season-wide unique participants by a one-week 32-by-53 roster denominator
